doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Closing words: a lot was done before you were born
summary: Woods and Brunious close with advice that young players should respect earlier artists and not chase fame.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: One thing someone said in terms of trying to show youngsters to respect people who’ve done more than they have is that little saying that says: a lot was done before you were born.
That sounds like a great parting line. A lot was done before you were born.
Yeah. And I know you’ve got to go. It’s been wonderful talking with you, and I think you’ve given some beautiful words of wisdom here.
I hope so. It helps some guys to realize, hey, you know, maybe I’d better take a little bit more inventory and stop trying to be famous within the first two years of my playing.
And the art is more precious than the trappings.
Thank you. We’ve been filming here our Jazz Archive interview with Wendell Brunious. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
